sync.title: Sync
sync.subtitle: Keep an encrypted backup of your workspace on Google Drive.
sync.conflictDescription: The local version and the Drive version differ. Choose the copy you want to keep.
sync.encryptedDescription: A single encrypted JSON file is uploaded to Google Drive. Google cannot read its contents.
sync.autoSyncDescription: Sync changes automatically when an internet connection is available.
sync.scopeDescription: The app uses the drive.file scope only to access its own file.
sync.disconnectConfirm: Google Drive will be disconnected. Your local data will remain unchanged.
sync.networkError: Could not connect to the network. Check your connection and try again.
sync.permissionError: Permission to access Google Drive was not granted.
sync.syncFileCreated: The encrypted backup file was created.

backup.title: Export & backups
backup.subtitle: Save an encrypted copy of your workspace in the Google Drive folder you choose.
backup.exportDescription: Choose a Drive destination and HSA Notes will write one JSON file encrypted with your vault key. No Google account connection or automatic access grant is used.
backup.localOnly: No Google account or OAuth required
backup.howItWorksDescription: Three simple steps, with no permanent access permissions.
backup.stepOne: Choose Save to Google Drive and select the destination folder.
backup.stepTwo: The app collects and encrypts your data locally before writing it.
backup.stepThree: Keep the file in Drive or import it later from Settings.
backup.pickerSupported: Your browser can choose a Drive folder directly from the save dialog.
backup.pickerFallback: Your browser will download the file instead of opening a Drive folder picker.
backup.exportSuccess: The encrypted backup was created and saved successfully.
backup.exportError: The backup file could not be created.

settings.passwordUpdateError: Could not change the password. Check the details you entered.

settings.deleteDataWarning: All keys, credentials, and notes will be permanently deleted.
settings.clientEncryptionNote: Client-side encryption provides strong protection for personal use, but it is not a substitute for an approved enterprise password manager for extremely sensitive data.
